name: Soft and Hard Cleft Palate
aliases: Cleft Palate involving Soft and Hard Palate
Combined Soft and Hard Palate Cleft

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in Asian and Native American populations

criteria.description: Visible fissure or opening involving both soft and hard palate on oral examination
Difficulty with feeding due to inability to create suction
Regurgitation of fluids through the nose during feeding
Speech abnormalities including hypernasality and articulation difficulties

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a visible cleft involving both soft and hard palate on clinical examination
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging and genetic testing may assist in associated syndromic cases.

imaging: CT or MRI for detailed palatal and craniofacial anatomy
genetic: Genetic testing for syndromic associations (e.g., 22q11.2 deletion syndrome)
Family history assessment for inherited clefting disorders

distinguishingFeatures: Cleft limited to soft palate without involvement of hard palate
Presence of cleft lip visible externally
May or may not involve palate
Intact mucosal surface with underlying muscular defect
Less obvious visual cleft, diagnosed by palpation or nasopharyngoscopy

redFlags: Inability to feed leading to failure to thrive
Severe speech delay or absence of speech development
references: Mossey PA, Little J, Munger RG, Dixon MJ, Shaw WC. Cleft lip and palate. Lancet. 2009 Nov 21;374(9703):1773-85.
Orphanet: Soft and Hard Cleft Palate - ORPHA:664372
American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association (ACPA) Clinical Standards
